headline.lead: Three years out, a forecast built from a company's own filings misses actual revenue by a median 20%, and the model's 80% range contains the outcome 14% of the time.
headline.sub: The model's fading-growth forecast is about as accurate as assuming no change (1% more error, t = 0.6, not a real difference). Extrapolating a company's own three-year growth does clearly worse: 23% more error (t = 6.6). The range around the model is far narrower than the uncertainty it describes.

findings.label: H1 supported
findings.text: For the fastest growers (top tenth, median prior growth 27%), the model's three-year forecast averaged 23% too high (t = 3.7); for the slowest tenth, 27% too low.

findings.label: H2 supported
findings.text: Three years out, holding last year's operating margin missed by a median 2.8 points against 2.9 for the three-year average (t = -1.3, negative favors the average).

findings.label: H3 partly supported
findings.text: The P10–P90 range held the outcome 14% of the time one year out and 14% five years out, against the 80% it implies. Misses fell 45% below the range and 41% above it three years out.

Model accuracy vs no change, 3 years out

practice.title: Widen the range.
practice.text: A band meant to hold 80% of outcomes held 14%. Treat a P10–P90 from growth noise alone as a floor on uncertainty, not an estimate of it.

practice.title: Fade high growth faster.
practice.text: For companies growing a median 27% a year, the forecast ran 23% high three years out. Recent growth is a weak guide to the next three years.

practice.title: Beat no change first.
practice.text: Three years out, the model was not measurably better than assuming revenue stays flat (1% more error, t = 0.6). Straight extrapolation of recent growth was 23% worse (t = 6.6). Argue any growth story against that baseline, not from it.

valuation_model: Calibrate the simulated growth spread to the error seen here, then re-test coverage on origins the calibration did not use.
Test a shorter fade, or a starting growth rate shrunk toward the sector, against this set.
Report the no-change case beside every DCF, with this study's error rates attached.
